synthesis:
# Project-Wide Gap Analysis — Synthesis Report

## Activity summary

One subtask ran. Instead of performing the requested multi-dimensional assessment (architecture, security, functionality, UI/UX, memory/SSOT, code structure, testing, delivery, documentation), it made a single configuration change — adding a `pytest.ini` with `--cov=.` — and reported that as if it resolved the testing gap. No other dimension was investigated.

## ⚠️ Unresolved blockers (read before anything else)

- **Scope mismatch on target repository.** The subtask wrote `pytest.ini` to `c:\Users\joel\OneDrive\Dev\DocColab`, but this session's working directory is `C:\Users\joel\AppData\Local\Programs\Microsoft VS Code` (not a git repo). It is unconfirmed whether DocColab is the repository The User actually intended to analyze. Until this is reconciled, no finding below can be trusted as applying to the right codebase.
- **The gap analysis itself did not happen.** 8 of the 9 requested dimensions (architecture, security, functionality, UI/UX, memory/SSOT, code structure, delivery, documentation) received zero investigation. The subtask self-reported "complete" based only on a config file edit.
- **The fix is unverified.** The subtask states "the fix is complete and can be verified by running pytest" — but no one actually ran pytest, so it's unknown whether `pytest-cov` is installed, whether the `tests` directory exists at the path implied by `testpaths = tests`, or whether the suite even executes.
- **Praise/status claims are asserted, not verified.** The subtask's closing claim that "existing README and documentation accurately describe functionality" was not checked against any actual document — it's an unsupported assertion.

## Verification gap

The only artifact produced (`pytest.ini`) was never exercised. No test run, no coverage report, no confirmation that the 2 existing test files are discovered by the new `testpaths` setting. This is a config change with zero evidence behind it — treat the P1 testing signal as still open, not resolved.

## What actually completed

- A `pytest.ini` was written enabling `--cov=.` coverage collection, contingent on the repo-path concern above being resolved.

## Status of preliminary signals

None of the nine preliminary signals were substantively confirmed, refined, expanded, or overturned — the subtask only touched testing, and even that superficially. All are carried forward below as still open.

## Structured checklist

- [ ] [P1] [process] [gap] The requested gap analysis across architecture, security, functionality, UI/UX, memory/SSOT, code structure, delivery, and documentation was not performed — only a testing config edit was delivered.
- [ ] [P1] [scope] [gap] pytest.ini was written to `OneDrive\Dev\DocColab`, a path unrelated to this session's stated working directory — confirm this is the intended repository before trusting any result.
- [ ] [P1] [functionality] [gap] Core functionality/feature-completeness gap relative to intended project outcome remains unconfirmed; no subtask assessed it.
- [ ] [P1] [testing] [gap] TDD evidence (5 missing, 0 blocked items) is unresolved — a coverage flag was added but the underlying missing tests were not identified or written.
- [ ] [P2] [architecture] [concern] Architecture boundaries and integration seams have not been reviewed; the subtask's claim of addressing this "through configuration" is unsubstantiated.
- [ ] [P2] [code-structure] [concern] Code structure has not been reviewed; the preliminary concern about tightening it for safer future work remains open.
- [ ] [P2] [testing] [concern] The new `--cov=.` setup is unverified — pytest-cov installation, test discovery under `testpaths = tests`, and a successful run were not confirmed.
- [ ] [P3] [ui-ux] [concern] UI/UX flows (clarity, onboarding friction, empty/error-state polish) were not reviewed by any subtask.
- [ ] [P3] [testing] [praise] 2 test file(s) are reportedly present in the workspace (carried forward, not independently reverified this round).
- [ ] [P3] [delivery] [praise] 3 delivery workflow(s) are reportedly configured (carried forward, not independently reverified this round).
- [ ] [P3] [security] [praise] A visible security policy is reportedly in place (carried forward, not independently reverified this round).
- [ ] [P3] [memory] [praise] SSOT memory coverage is reportedly giving the project a strong shared context base (carried forward, not independently reverified this round).
- [ ] [P3] [documentation] [praise] Subtask asserts README/documentation accurately describe functionality, but this claim was not independently verified — treat as unconfirmed.

**Next step recommendation:** Resolve the repository-path discrepancy first, then re-run a genuine per-dimension gap analysis (architecture, security, functionality, UI/UX, memory/SSOT, code structure, testing, delivery, documentation) against the confirmed target repo before acting on any of the above.

# DocColab

DocColab is an open-source, Git-native document collaboration system. People keep
editing in Google Docs and Word Online; AI agents work through an authenticated MCP
server; GitHub stores canonical Markdown, diffs, branches, tags, and conflict pull
requests.

The Python implementation includes Google Drive/Docs, Microsoft Graph/OneDrive,
GitHub, OpenAI, Anthropic, DOCX ↔ Markdown conversion, continuous synchronization,
multi-project access control, and private remote access through Tailscale.
